1. Title: SQL Injection via String Concatenation
   Category: Confirmed Vulnerability
   Severity: High
   Confidence: High
   File: <user_code>
   Line: 15
   Evidence: The query `q = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"` constructs a SQL query using string concatenation of the user-supplied input `name` without any parameterization or sanitization.
   Data Flow: `request.args.get("name")` (Source) → String Concatenation → `db.execute(q)` (Sink)
   Why It Matters: An attacker can manipulate the `name` parameter to inject SQL logic (e.g., `' OR '1'='1`) to bypass authentication or dump the entire database.
   Why It Was Detected: Direct string concatenation feeding a database execution sink.
   Recommended Fix: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements).
   Manual Verification Required: Yes — verify the database schema and whether authentication relies on this query.
   Vulnerable Code: q = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'"
   Fixed Code: q = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?" ; db.execute(q, (name,))

2. Title: Command Injection via Subprocess Shell Execution
   Category: Confirmed Vulnerability
   Severity: High
   Confidence: High
   File: <user_code>
   Line: 22
   Evidence: The command `subprocess.run("ping -c 1 " + host, shell=True, ...)` constructs a shell command dynamically using the user-controlled input `host` and executes it with `shell=True`.
   Data Flow: `request.args.get("host")` (Source) → String Concatenation → `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)` (Sink)
   Why It Matters: An attacker can inject shell metacharacters (e.g., `; rm -rf /`) to execute arbitrary system commands on the server.
   Why It Was Detected: Dynamic command construction with `shell=True` allows untrusted input to reach the shell interpreter.
   Recommended Fix: Avoid `shell=True` and use a list for arguments, or use `shlex.quote()` if shell features are strictly required.
   Manual Verification Required: Yes — verify the environment and permissions of the web server user.
   Vulnerable Code: output = subprocess.run("ping -c 1 " + host, shell=True, capture_output=True)
   Fixed Code: output = subprocess.run(["ping", "-c", "1", host], capture_output=True)

3. Title: Unsafe Deserialization of Pickle Data
   Category: Confirmed Vulnerability
   Severity: High
   Confidence: High
   File: <user_code>
   Line: 28
   Evidence: The code calls `pickle.loads(request.data)` without any validation or whitelisting of the input source.
   Data Flow: `request.data` (Source) → `pickle.loads()` (Sink)
   Why It Matters: The `pickle` module is not secure against erroneous or maliciously constructed data. An attacker can craft a pickle payload that executes arbitrary code upon deserialization.
   Why It Was Detected: Direct use of `pickle.loads` on untrusted request data.
   Recommended Fix: Do not use `pickle` for web data exchange. Use JSON or MessagePack with a safe parser.
   Manual Verification Required: Yes — verify if this endpoint is exposed to untrusted users.
   Vulnerable Code: obj = pickle.loads(request.data)
   Fixed Code: import json; obj = json.loads(request.data)

4. Title: Path Traversal in File Read Operation
   Category: Confirmed Vulnerability
   Severity: Medium
   Confidence: High
   File: <user_code>
   Line: 38
   Evidence: The path `path = "/var/data/" + request.args.get("name")` concatenates user input directly into a filesystem path without normalization or validation.
   Data Flow: `request.args.get("name")` (Source) → String Concatenation → `open(path)` (Sink)
   Why It Matters: An attacker can request `../../etc/passwd` to read arbitrary files on the server, potentially exposing sensitive configuration or credentials.
   Why It Was Detected: Unsanitized user input appended to a base path before a filesystem operation.
   Recommended Fix: Use `os.path.join()` for path construction and validate the final path against a whitelist.
   Manual Verification Required: Yes — verify what files exist in `/var/data/` and the permissions of the web server.
   Vulnerable Code: path = "/var/data/" + request.args.get("name")
   Fixed Code: base_path = "/var/data/"; safe_name = os.path.basename(request.args.get("name", "")); path = os.path.join(base_path, safe_name)

5. Title: Hardcoded Secret Credential
   Category: Potential Vulnerability
   Severity: Medium
   Confidence: High
   File: <user_code>
   Line: 32
   Evidence: A variable `ADMIN_TOKEN` is assigned a masked secret value (`sk-***********************************4c`).
   Data Flow: Assignment → (Usage unknown)
   Why It Matters: Hardcoded secrets are a major security risk. If this token is used for authentication and the code is committed to a public repository, the secret is compromised.
   Why It Was Detected: Assignment of a masked secret string.
   Recommended Fix: Load secrets from environment variables or a secure vault (e.g., `os.getenv("ADMIN_TOKEN")`).
   Manual Verification Required: Yes — verify if this token is actually used for authentication or authorization.
   Vulnerable Code: ADMIN_TOKEN = "sk-***********************************4c"
   Fixed Code: ADMIN_TOKEN = os.getenv("ADMIN_TOKEN")
